brief:
South Africa has submitted evidence to a dedicated judicial committee accusing Israel of violating legally binding provisional measures ordered by the International Court of Justice, the Middle East Eye reported. Pretoria argues that Israel has defied the court's mandates in an ongoing manner, challenging the state's compliance record before the specialized panel.

The submission represents South Africa's formal escalation of its case against Israel at the world court. The filing centers on whether Israel has adhered to specific directives issued by the ICJ in provisional measures—orders that carry legal force and bind parties to compliance. South Africa's presentation of evidence to the committee signals its intent to hold Israel accountable for any breaches of those court-ordered obligations.
